target.title: feat(hooks): allow a dedicated queue lane per hook mapping
target.body:
Related: #43235

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where hook-triggered isolated agent runs all share the single global cron command lane. In deployments that drive latency-sensitive automation through webhooks (e.g. an issue-tracker pickup hook), those runs queue behind unrelated hook and scheduled-cron traffic — we observed accepted webhook runs waiting 40+ minutes for a lane slot while the target session lane sat idle.

This implements a per-hook-mapping slice of the ask in #43235 (per-agent/dedicated command lanes for multi-agent deployments). A previous broader attempt was #73991 (closed).

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds an optional `hooks.mappings[].lane` config field so operators can route a class of hooks onto a dedicated command-queue lane, instead of widening global concurrency. Boundaries: the default stays `cron` (zero behavior change unless configured), and the lane override is trusted config/mapping-only — external `/hooks/agent` request payloads cannot mint arbitrary lanes (covered by a test that posts a payload-supplied lane and asserts it is ignored).

## User Impact

Operators running multi-hook/multi-agent gateways can keep latency-sensitive hook automations from waiting behind generic hook/cron traffic by setting `lane` on the relevant mapping. Deployments that don't opt in see no change.

## Evidence

- AI-assisted: yes (written with an LLM coding agent; reviewed and validated before submission — I understand what the code does).
- On the original branch base: `vitest run src/gateway/server.hooks.test.ts src/gateway/hooks-mapping.test.ts src/config/config.hooks-module-paths.test.ts src/config/schema.help.quality.test.ts` — 164 tests passed; `config:schema:check` passed; tsgo typecheck passed.
- New test: `routes hook agent runs through an explicit lane when configured` (mapped hook lands on its configured lane; direct payload-supplied lane is rejected back to `cron`).
- This branch is the same patch cherry-picked cleanly onto current `main` (identical numstat); relying on CI here for fresh validation against tip.


## Real behavior proof (after-fix, real gateway from this branch)

Throwaway OpenClaw gateway built from this branch's source (`pnpm build` at `4be6e01`), run headless on Linux (Node 22) with an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, hooks enabled, and a live OpenAI-compatible model behind a LiteLLM proxy (endpoint/tokens redacted). Config carries exactly one mapping with the new field:

```json5
hooks: {
  enabled: true,
  token: "<redacted>",
  mappings: [
    {
      match: { path: "jira-pickup" },
      action: "agent",
      name: "Jira Pickup",
      messageTemplate: "Reply with exactly the single word ACK for {{payload.issue.key}}. Do not use any tools.",
      lane: "jira-pickup",   // <-- new field under test
      deliver: false,
    },
  ],
}
```

**Call 1 — direct `/hooks/agent`, payload tries to mint a lane (must be ignored):**

```text
$ curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:18999/hooks/agent \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"message":"Reply with exactly the single word ACK. Do not use any tools.","lane":"attacker-minted-lane","deliver":false}'
{"ok":true,"runId":"1cd8fbf8-5824-44fd-a07e-892a9beaebc3"}
```

**Call 2 — mapped `/hooks/jira-pickup`, lane configured on the mapping:**

```text
$ curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:18999/hooks/jira-pickup \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"issue":{"key":"FAD-1526"}}'
{"ok":true,"runId":"c56e4a6d-9c37-449c-b3fe-a1ca2130eff3"}
```

**Lane routing observed in the gateway's diagnostic log** (`queue.lane.enqueue`, one isolated hook agent run each):

```text
2026-07-02T01:02:50.856-05:00  DEBUG [diagnostic]  lane enqueue: lane=cron-nested queueSize=1   <- call 1: payload lane IGNORED, stays on the default cron lane (resolved cron -> cron-nested)
2026-07-02T01:03:17.392-05:00  DEBUG [diagnostic]  lane enqueue: lane=jira-pickup queueSize=1   <- call 2: mapping-configured lane honored
```

`grep -c "attacker-minted-lane"` across the gateway console log and the diagnostic file log: **0 occurrences** — the payload-supplied lane never reaches any queue, log line, or config surface.

**Both runs completed normally** on the branch build (streamed model responses, hook runs finished; `deliver:false` so no channel announcement is expected):

```text
2026-07-02T01:02:51.186-05:00 [provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] start provider=litellm api=openai-completions model=<redacted> method=POST url=<redacted>/v1/chat/completions
2026-07-02T01:02:52.681-05:00 [provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] response provider=litellm api=openai-completions model=<redacted> status=200 elapsedMs=1489 contentType=text/event-stream
2026-07-02T01:02:52.785-05:00 [hooks] hook agent run completed without announcement
2026-07-02T01:03:17.665-05:00 [provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] start provider=litellm api=openai-completions model=<redacted> method=POST url=<redacted>/v1/chat/completions
2026-07-02T01:03:19.868-05:00 [provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] response provider=litellm api=openai-completions model=<redacted> status=200 elapsedMs=2197 contentType=text/event-stream
2026-07-02T01:03:19.942-05:00 [hooks] hook agent run completed without announcement
```

Call 1 doubles as the unchanged-default evidence: a hook with no `lane` configured (and even a hostile payload `lane`) still lands on the shared `cron` lane exactly as on `main`. The proof harness (throwaway config + curl) is intentionally not part of the committed diff.
